Edit 3: Translation of medical jargon:

  • Diabetes mellitus - Greater than 80 percent of cases of type II diabetes can be attributed to obesity.
  • Dyslipidemia - Abnormalities in cholesterol metabolism which are not simply limited to "high cholesterol." Abnormal ratios of LDL, VLDL, and HDL which increase the risk of coronary artery disease even in the presence of a "normal" overall cholesterol level.
  • Gout - Gout is mostly thought of as a punchline, but it is a destructive arthritis that can destroy joints.
  • Heart failure - 5 percent for men and 7 percent for women increase in the risk of heart failure, INDEPENDENT of the degree of coronary artery disease.
  • Myocardial steatosis - Deposition of lipids in the heart musculature which can lead to left ventricular hypertrophy, negatively affecting the function of the heart.
  • Atrial fibrillation/flutter - Abnormal heart rhythms which can have debilitating and/or lethal consequences.
  • Stroke - Increased risk of stroke INDEPENDENT of cholesterol, blood pressure, diabetes
  • Hepatobiliary disease - Gallstones and gallstone related complications are the primary way in which obesity affects the liver and biliary system. Non Alcoholic Related Steatosis (NASH) is also related to obesity and can cause a severe hepatitis and even result in cirrhosis.
  • GERD - Gastrointestinal reflux disease (heartburn) and its associated complications, including erosions of the esophagus, esophageal and gastric cancer.
  • Osteoarthritis - Our bones and cartilage did not evolve to support the weight of the obese. This is most common in the lower extremities (knees and ankles). It also occurs in non-weight-bearing joints, so there may be a hormonal/metabolic component of obesity contributing.
  • Infection - This includes skin and soft tissue infections, postoperative infections, and respiratory infections.
  • Respiratory system - Sleep apnea is a major associated complication. Lung volumes are also decreased at higher weights due to the weight of the chest wall pushing down on the lungs.
  • Kidney disease - Increased incidence of chronic kidney disease that is SEPARATE from hypertension and diabetes.
